title: Hesperus flow 0.2
description: What happens when a program is entered: for each entry point, the functions it reaches in source order and where each path leaves the program. Emitted by an extractor next to the actual IR (`.hesperus/actual/flow.json`), read by the viewer's Flow mode. Separate from the IR: nothing here is diffed. Nothing is inferred: names come from declarations, order from source position, boundaries from the same rule table as the actual, and a call is a step only when its callee resolves to a declaration in the repository.

root.description: Root node id of the actual IR this flow belongs to.

depth.description: Calls followed from an entry before a step is cut with `depth`.

steps.description: Steps recorded per entry before the rest is cut with `steps`.

components.description: Every node the flow names (owners of units, boundaries, constraint ends), as the intent names them; sorted by id.

kind.description: The intent node's kind, or the boundary kind of the crossing that named it.

units.description: Every function the entries reach, sorted by id.

entries.description: Entry points in evidence order (path, then line).

constraints.description: The intent's `require` and `forbid` lines checked against every function in the repository, reached by an entry or not. A witness is a site inside `from` that reaches `to`: a crossing to a boundary within `to` with the edge kind (any kind when null; `unknown` store access counts for `reads` and `writes`), or a call to a function owned by a node within `to` (kind `calls` or null).

entries.description: Ids of the entries whose paths pass through the function holding the site; empty when no entry reaches it.

unitId.description: `file#name`: `Class.method` for methods, `<module>` for a file's top-level code, `anonymous` for an inline handler; `@line` is appended when a file declares the name twice.

name.description: Declared name as written in the code.

owner.description: Id of the actual node that owns the file: the intent node whose `src` binds it, else the unbound node for its directory. The same bindings the actual IR uses.

id.description: `kind:unit`, with `@n` appended when one function serves several entries.

kind.description: route: a handler registered on an ingress the rule table recognizes (or the function holding a pathname comparison); main: a `main` function that is exported or called at the top level; module: the top-level code of a `bin` file or a file with a shebang; command: a CLI command handler (commander/cac/yargs/citty style `.action(fn)`, `.command(..., fn)`, `defineCommand({ run })`); export: an exported function a host calls by name (`activate`/`deactivate` in a file importing `vscode`).

label.description: `GET /users`, `MATCH /x`, `main`, the file name, `command <name>`, or the export name.

at.description: Where the entry is registered or declared.

call.description: A call to a function in the repository, in source order within its caller.

steps.description: The callee's steps; absent when cut.

cut.description: Why the callee is not expanded here: it is on the current call path; it was expanded earlier in this entry; the depth limit; the step budget.

crossing.description: Where a path leaves the program, classified by the rule table.

node.description: Node id in the actual IR (adopted from the intent when a binding matches).

label.description: The intent label when bound, else the host, engine, route or resource name.

edge.description: `unknown`: a store access whose SQL verb or method the rules could not classify.

resolved.description: False for `network unresolved` targets and `unknown` store access.
